name: slides-notebook
description: Opens the markdown of a slides-rs deck as a notebook, runs its code cells as the deck does, and saves their outputs where the deck reads them.

commands.title: Collapse or Expand the Steps' Column

colors.description: The background of the line where a slide of a deck's markdown begins: its rule, or an import.
The background of a slide's title, a `#` heading, in a deck's markdown.
The background of a subtitle, a `##` heading, in a deck's markdown.
The background of a column's heading, a `###`, in a deck's markdown.
The line down a column of a deck's markdown, before its text.
The line down every other column of a deck's markdown, beside the one before, before its text.
The steps written before a line of a deck's markdown that steps.
The background of the column the steps are written in, before the lines of a deck's markdown.
The background of every other slide of a deck's markdown, so that two in a row tell apart.

slides.editor.alternateSlides.markdownDescription: Shade every other slide of a deck's markdown, in `slides.alternateSlide`.

slides.editor.headings.markdownDescription: Highlight a slide's title (`#`), its subtitles (`##`) and its columns' headings (`###`), each in a color of its own: `slides.title`, `slides.subtitle` and `slides.columnHeading`.

slides.editor.columns.markdownDescription: Draw a line down each column, from its `###` to the next, before its text, in `slides.column` and `slides.alternateColumn` by turns.

slides.editor.steps.markdownDescription: Write before each line that steps, in a column of their own, in `slides.stepColumn`, the steps it shows in, as the deck numbers them: `3` from the third on, `2..4` up to the fourth, and a `*` if it takes no space while hidden. And above each slide, how many steps it has, which collapses or expands the column, as hovering over it does.

slides.pythonServer.markdownDescription: The Python language server for the code cells in the markdown text editor, started in the environment they run in: a command, such as `basedpyright-langserver`, `ty` or `pyright-langserver`, or its path. Empty, the one the editor has for Python: that of the ty, basedpyright or Pyright extension, or Jedi if `python.languageServer` says so, installed in that environment or on the `PATH`, or else as its extension bundles it; or else the first of those commands installed. `off`, or with none found, as with Pylance, the cells are asked of the Python language server VS Code has, with no diagnostics.

slides.path.markdownDescription: The `slides-rs` command, which runs the code cells with `slides-rs kernel`. Empty, the one that comes with the extension, or else `slides-rs` on the `PATH`.
